name: Aurofex Builder
author: Jose Mortellaro

sections.description:
Design pages, posts, and the whole site from a visual editor in WordPress admin — the kind of panel people expect from a page builder. Visitors never load that editor.

Aurofex Builder writes normal Gutenberg blocks. The public page is the HTML WordPress already knows how to render. There is no builder stylesheet, no builder runtime, and no shortcode left behind for the theme to interpret.

Turn the plugin off. The layout stays. Header, footer, pages, and posts keep rendering, because nothing on the front end belonged to the plugin in the first place.

That is the point. You edit visually. The site you publish does not pay for the editor.

What you get

  • A visual builder for pages, posts, and the Site Editor, only in wp-admin.
  • Native block markup, so the content remains yours.
  • A public site that does not load the builder.
  • A layout that survives deactivation.

What the public site does not get

No extra CSS framework. No editor JavaScript. No lock-in. Deactivate Aurofex Builder and open the front end: the page is still there.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/aurofex-builder directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open a page, a post, or the Site Editor. The visual builder is available in the block editor.
sections.faq:
Does the public site depend on the plugin?

No. Pages are stored as Gutenberg blocks. WordPress renders them with or without Aurofex Builder. Deactivate the plugin and the front end keeps working.

Does it add anything to the front end while it is active?

The page itself does not. The builder’s CSS and JavaScript load only in the admin.

While the plugin is active it prints one short inline script that toggles a scrolled class on the html element after the visitor scrolls. If no other plugin has already printed them, it can also add the document title, a meta description from the excerpt, and social sharing tags taken from the post. None of that is required for the layout. Turn the plugin off and those extras go away with it. The blocks stay.

Will my pages break if I uninstall it?

The content will not. It is ordinary block markup. Another editor, the Site Editor, or the theme can keep displaying it.
